Why isn’t anyone in Maine demanding an investigation and/or prosecution of Graham Platner for rape? It’s well within the statute of limitations. If Dems really believe he’s a rapist, why is the only penalty he can’t run for senate? With @CharlesHurt:

I haven’t even heard one person calling for a prosecution. Or even an investigation. Seems significant. Otherwise you’re admitting that the allegation isn’t actually disqualifying at all. Which Platner himself should be arguing. This entire story is a mountain of stupid illogic.

Right. But if they don’t want him behind bars doesn’t that mean they know he didn’t actually commit rape? (Which would mean the allegation isn’t really disqualifying.) If someone is actually a rapist, I don’t just want to keep them from a good job, I want them behind bars.

Final point, if I’m Graham Platner, I would have gone on video, denied all charges, welcomed the investigation, and said if I’m charged and convicted, I’ll resign. That’s the checkmate move for him. This entire story just makes zero sense. Both from state, media and candidate.

Which makes me wonder two things: one, are the odds of a conviction truly zero, making the allegations a stand alone disqualifier? Or two, are Dems, who run the state, implicitly or explicitly, telling him this goes away if he drops out, but charges come if he doesn’t?

The standard seems to be — the rape accusation itself is disqualifying. I disagree with that standard, as I have said. But if you actually rape someone you should be charged and a jury should determine your fate. Why are no Dems demanding this? Why is almost no one?

If Graham Platner committed rape five years ago in Maine, why is no one demanding he be charged with rape? The statute of limitations is, crazily, twenty years in Maine. The alleged rape was five years ago. Yet no one is demanding charges. Or even an investigation. Why is that?
